questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-{b}_{2}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{3}$ and ${c}_{3}={b}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}+6{b}_{3} \\  & =-3{b}_{2}+6{b}_{3}+{b}_{1} \\  & =3(-{b}_{2})+3(2{b}_{3})+{b}_{1} \\  & =3{c}_{1}+3{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=4(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-7{b}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}-7({c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}-7{c}_{1}+14{c}_{2} \\  & =-7{c}_{1}+\frac{29}{2}{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ \frac{29}{2}\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-3{b}_{2}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{3}$ and ${c}_{3}=3{b}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}-2{b}_{3} \\  & =6{b}_{2}-2{b}_{3}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-2(-3{b}_{2})-2{b}_{3}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=-\frac{1}{4}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-8{b}_{1}+6{b}_{2} \\  & =-8(-\frac{1}{4}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})+6(-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1} \\  & =-{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
